title: Salaman and Absal
author: jami
attributionNote: The attribution is not disputed in the scholarship this catalogue follows.
description: Jami's allegorical poem of the prince Salaman and his nurse Absal, whose love ends in separation and whose story is read as the soul's attachment to the world of sense. FitzGerald's English rendering, in the metre he had used for Omar Khayyam, compresses the narrative and makes the allegory explicit in its prologue and closing sections.
historicalContext: Written by the last great classical Persian poet, who died in Herat in 1492. FitzGerald published his anonymous verse translation in 1856, twenty-three years before his Rubaiyat; the Gutenberg edition prints it with the Rubaiyat and FitzGerald's life.
availabilityNote: Streamed from Project Gutenberg at read time: the whole plain-text edition is fetched and split at the chapter headings it prints. The 1856 translation by Edward FitzGerald is public domain in the United States.
